entries.title: POP/STARS (Instrumental)
entries.usedFor: Official instrumental of K/DA's debut single
entries.background: The vocal-free version of POP/STARS, the song that introduced K/DA (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai'Sa) at the 2018 World Championship opening ceremony. Riot added it to the League of Legends SoundCloud three days after the single, completing a two-track K/DA - POP/STARS set; it was never issued as a separate streaming release.

sources.title: K/DA - POP/STARS [Instrumental] (League of Legends SoundCloud, uploaded 2018-11-06)

POP/STARS (SoundCloud release with instrumental) - MusicBrainz

entries.notes: Official instrumental published only on the League of Legends SoundCloud; it is not on Spotify and no official YouTube upload was found, so audioYoutubeId is null. Cover: the POP/STARS single art, identical to the SoundCloud artwork.

entries.title: GIANTS (Instrumental)
entries.usedFor: Official instrumental of True Damage's debut single
entries.background: The instrumental of GIANTS, the debut single of True Damage, the hip-hop group of Akali, Ekko, Qiyana, Senna and Yasuo. Riot uploaded it to the League of Legends SoundCloud on 10 November 2019, the day the group premiered the song live at the Worlds 2019 Finals in Paris.

entries.notes: Official instrumental published only on the League of Legends SoundCloud; it is not on Spotify and no official YouTube upload was found, so audioYoutubeId is null. Cover: the GIANTS single art, identical to the SoundCloud artwork. Producer credit not verified, so only True Damage is listed.

entries.title: Childhood Dreams
entries.usedFor: Seraphine's first release, a pre-launch cover
entries.background: Seraphine's first released song: a cover of Norwegian singer ARY's 2017 single, posted on the in-character SoundCloud (seradotwav) that Riot ran for her months before she was revealed as a League champion. Jasmine Clarke, Seraphine's singing voice, recorded it with Absofacto; it reached streaming services on 25 September 2020.

entries.notes: Date is the SoundCloud upload; Spotify/YouTube Music carry 2020-09-25. Two Spotify copies exist (3wwemGboQqYJOMYwNE9DIX is the one on the artist's top tracks; 0NBkXEbOvbGyUgPHVdW3k1 is a duplicate) and two Topic art tracks (2y9nE6E1cow, listed on the Seraphine - Topic channel, and bQCg73ox1Rc). Absofacto is credited on the cover art ('with Jasmine Clarke, Absofacto'), not in the Spotify artist list.

entries.title: All The Things She Said
entries.background: Seraphine's take on t.A.T.u.'s 2002 hit, the third cover from her pre-launch SoundCloud run, made with Jasmine Clarke, Absofacto and Kosuke Kasza. It appeared on SoundCloud and on streaming services on the same day, about a month before her debut with K/DA on MORE.

entries.title: Made Me This Way
entries.background: The only original song from Seraphine's pre-launch SoundCloud era, written and recorded with Jasmine Clarke, Absofacto, Kosuke Kasza, Sophia Alexa and Chris Zane. It came out less than two weeks before K/DA's MORE, the single that introduced Seraphine as a K/DA collaborator, and her arrival as a playable champion.

entries.title: Predator (World Ender Remix)
entries.background: A reworked Predator from Pentakill III: Lost Chapter, released by Riot as a single and as official audio on the Legends of Runeterra channel for its Worlds 2022 celebration. It arrived shortly before the Darkin Saga: World Ender expansion and the LoR World Championship of December 2022, with the original's singers Tre Watson and TELLE joined by Mark Evans.

entries.title: Know My Name (Instrumental)
entries.background: The official instrumental of Know My Name, True Damage's comeback single and the Worlds 2026 anthem. Riot posted it on the League of Legends SoundCloud on release night, next to a SoundCloud remix contest that offered fans the official stems to rework the anthem until 28 October 2026.

entries.notes: Official instrumental published only on the League of Legends SoundCloud; it is not on Spotify and no official YouTube upload was found, so audioYoutubeId is null. SoundCloud upload time is 2026-10-09 01:01 UTC (evening of 8 October in Los Angeles) and its release-date metadata is 2026-10-08. Production credit for Sebastien Najand comes from the Worlds 2026 anthem announcement summarized in data/curated/news.json.
